brief:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu criticized five opposition leaders for forming a coalition ahead of Israel's October 27 elections, according to Al Jazeera English. The opposition parties agreed to cooperate in an effort to increase voter turnout and secure a parliamentary majority.

Netanyahu's comments came as the opposition sought to coordinate their electoral strategy to challenge his government's hold on power.
dek: Five opposition leaders agree to cooperate to boost voter turnout to secure a majority in the October 27 elections.
title: Netanyahu attacks opposition leaders uniting for October elections
